html:
The Djab wurrung are an Aboriginal Australian people of western Victoria, whose country lies around today's Ararat and the eastern side of Gariwerd, the Grampians.

Their neighbours were the Jardwadjali to the west, the Gunditjmara and Girai wurrung to the south and the Dja Dja Wurrung to the east. Gariwerd holds many rock art sites.

Squatters took the western plains in the late 1830s and 1840s. In the Victorian gold rush, Chinese miners found a rich lead at Ararat in 1857. Recent years saw a long protest to protect Djab wurrung birthing and directions trees from a highway widening; one directions tree was cut down in 2020.
sum: The Djab wurrung are an Aboriginal Australian people of western Victoria, whose country lies around today's Ararat and the eastern side of Gariwerd, the Grampians.
